features.text: Patient reports left knee instability that occasionally gives out when walking, with a sensation of potential falling but usually catching themselves.
Left knee instability occurs less than once a day and resolves quickly.
Left knee instability has been present for a few weeks.
No specific injury or incident preceded the onset of left knee instability.
No pain, swelling, or locking in the knee.
No specific activities or movements trigger the knee instability.
No prior similar issues with other joints or knees.
No neurological symptoms such as numbness, tingling, or weakness in the left leg or foot.
No recent episodes of dizziness or balance issues.
No prior orthopedic evaluations, imaging studies (e.g., MRI or X-ray), or physical examinations for the left knee.
No prior episodes of syncope, vertigo, or neurological symptoms in the lower extremity.
Knee instability occurs during normal walking, sometimes on flat ground, without specific triggers.
No prior orthopedic evaluations or imaging studies for the knee.
Patient is willing to undergo an orthopedic examination and imaging studies such as an MRI or X-ray.
No activities or movements make the instability worse or more frequent.
No weakness, numbness, or tingling in the leg or foot during episodes of instability.
No specific patterns or activities trigger the episodes of knee instability.
No pain, swelling, or sensation of the knee 'locking' during or after episodes of instability.
No previous imaging studies of the left knee or other joints.
No prior physical therapy evaluations or treatments for knee instability or related issues.
